title: If it happened tomorrow, would you be ready?
html:
Good morning,

Auguste Rodin said, “Patience is also a form of action.”

I've never thought of patience as an action before.

In fact, I've generally thought of it as the opposite. It was waiting around for something to happen.

But being patient can mean learning, preparing, building a foundation or waiting for the right opportunity.

You're getting ready.

Charles used to say you needed to “get ready to get ready”.

That came back to me when I read Rodin's quote. Sometimes there's work to do before you're even ready to take the next step. Learning what's involved. Making time. Getting yourself into a position where you can begin.

It's easy to get frustrated when something you want is taking longer than you hoped.

You want the results now!
The opportunity now!!
The success now!!!

But what if it arrived tomorrow?

Would you actually be ready?

It's a question I'd rather ask myself now than have answered for me when an opportunity arrives and I can't make the most of it.

Perhaps there's a skill to develop, a conversation to have or something unfinished that needs my attention.

Patience gives me time to work on those things. But I still have to use it.

MondayMotivator

Use the waiting time to prepare for what you want. Get ready to get ready.

Weekly Prompt

What's one thing you can do this week to be better prepared for something you're waiting for?

To your success!

Glenn "The Consistent Cash Man" Edley
